messages:
Marta C: Heads-up — after upgrading the JS SDK to v2.4.0 we hit hard runtime errors on Next edge builds (Vercel). Stack points at an interop helper that looks like it got tree-shaken away.

Marta C: stacktrace snippet:
```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'rewrite')
    at e.exports (dist/cjs/runtime/index.js:23:12)
    at async EdgeHandler (server/edge-handler.js:45:7)
```

Alex: ugh. do you have the package.json and exports/sideEffects info?

Marta C: package.json has "sideEffects": false and our exports map has both cjs and esm entries. snippet:
```json
"exports": {".": {"require": "./dist/cjs/index.js", "import": "./dist/esm/index.js"}},
"sideEffects": false
```

Sam: are you using SWC/Turbopack on Vercel or a custom bundler?

Marta C: default Vercel edge build: SWC + Turbopack. Works fine on node server builds, only edge runtime fails at runtime.

Lina: this reads like SWC's DCE + sideEffects:false pruning removed a tiny runtime helper that the CJS entry relies on. In some bundlers the CJS->ESM interop helpers are considered dead if only the ESM entry is statically referenced.

Jamal: probable symptom: default import becomes undefined after tree-shake when interop helper was the only place referencing a side-effectful init. Also conditional exports can confuse bundlers into pulling only the esm path.

Marta C: repro steps I used: next app with edge api route importing default from our sdk: `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` then deploy to Vercel edge. Node build (server) works, edge crashes. Local reproduction with `next dev --turbo` shows same.

Alex: quick mitigation: add an explicit sideEffects whitelist for the runtime/init file in package.json, e.g. "sideEffects": ["dist/runtime/init.js"] so bundlers don't drop it. Also consider in ESM entry re-exporting the cjs default: `export { default as default } from '../cjs/index.js'` to preserve interop.

Sam: we should also add a tiny conditional import guard in the CJS entry that keeps the helper used from being tree-shaken, like `if (typeof globalThis.__REDWOOD_RUNTIME__ === 'undefined') { /* noop to force include */ }` — ugly but effective until we release proper fix.

Lina: longer term: update our published package to avoid relying on side-effectful initializers and add an integration test that bundles the SDK with SWC/Turbopack + edge runtime and runs a smoke route. Also document recommended import style for edge (named vs default).

Jamal: opened an issue with labels (edge, bundler, high): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4812 — includes replication steps + patch suggestion.

ci-bot: Created issue #4812 and linked PR template. (automated)

Marta C: I'm going to publish 2.4.1-canary with the sideEffects whitelist and a tiny init guard. Will post canary tag here once available for testing.

Alex: thanks — once canary is up let's test on a few internal next edge apps (growth, docs, demo).

Sam: also add a changelog note and a short blurb in the DX onboarding doc about ESM/CJS edge pitfalls.

Marta C: ack, will do. cc @Platform for possible console guidance on "recommended import" patterns.

Alex: :thumbsup:

Marta C: final note — types were unaffected (TS defs still fine) but runtime mismatch is what bit folks. keep that in mind when triaging future reports.
